description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Control Systems topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: control-systems

facts.claim: A transfer function models the output for each input (Laplace domain)

source.quote: is a mathematical function that models the system's output for each po

facts.claim: Parts are blocks joined by lines showing their relationships

source.quote: the principal parts or functions are represented by blocks connected by lines that show the relationships of the blocks

facts.claim: Nodes (variables) joined by directed branches with gains (transmittances)

source.quote: A linear SFG consists of nodes indicated by dots and weighted directional branches indicated by arrows

facts.claim: Named after Mason (Mason graph / gain formula)

source.quote: often called a Mason graph after Samuel Jefferson Mason

facts.claim: LTI state equations are written in matrix form

source.quote: the equations can be written in matrix form

facts.claim: State variables track how inputs shape behaviour over time

source.quote: uses state variables to track how inputs shape system behavior over

facts.claim: Step response: output when the input jumps from 0 to 1

source.quote: step response is the time behaviour of the outputs of a general system when its inputs change from zero to one in a very short time

facts.claim: Overshoot: the output exceeds its final steady-state value

source.quote: overshoot refers to an output exceeding its final, steady-state value

facts.claim: Integral action removes steady-state error

source.quote: The integral (I) component, in turn, considers the cumulative sum of past errors to address any residual steady-state errors

facts.claim: Derivative action uses the rate of change of error, reducing overshoot

source.quote: the derivative (D) component predicts future error trend by assessing the rate of change of the error

facts.claim: Every bounded input gives a bounded output

source.quote: the output will be bounded for every input to the system that is bounded

facts.claim: Stable when all roots lie in the left half-plane

source.quote: a polynomial has all roots in the open left half-plane if and only if all first-column elements of the Routh array have the same sign

facts.claim: Check sign changes in the first column of the Routh array

source.quote: all first-column elements of the Routh array have the same sign

facts.claim: Root locus plots closed-loop poles as the gain varies

source.quote: The root locus plots the poles of the closed loop transfer function in the complex s-plane as a function of a gain parameter

facts.claim: Magnitude (dB) and phase plots versus frequency

source.quote: a combination of a Bode magnitude plot, expressing the magnitude (usually in decibels) of the frequency response, and a Bode phase plot

facts.claim: Straight-line asymptotic approximations

source.quote: the plot is an asymptotic approximation of the frequency response, using straight line segments

facts.claim: Stability from encirclements of the −1 point

source.quote: Stability is determined by looking at the number of encirclements of the point (−1, 0)

facts.claim: It uses the open-loop frequency response

source.quote: it only looks at the Nyquist plot of the open loop systems

facts.claim: Lead adds phase at high frequencies; lag acts at low frequencies

source.quote: The lead compensator provides phase lead at high frequencies

facts.claim: Each adds a pole–zero pair

source.quote: Both lead compensators and lag compensators introduce a pole–zero pair into the open loop transfer function
